info.title: The Graph — subgraph query
info.summary: Query any subgraph published on The Graph Network over HTTP.
info.description:
The second half of tashan's composition, described so an agent platform can onboard it.

tashan measures whether a capability is well made. This measures whether anyone has paid for it — the x402 settlement index on Base, read from a subgraph published on The Graph Network. Neither half answers the question alone, which is the point: the interesting rows are the ones where quality and payment disagree.

This is a thin description of one operation: POST a GraphQL query to a subgraph by id. It exists so a Recipe can bind The Graph as a tool alongside tashan's own, rather than us re-serving their data and calling it ours.

post.summary: Run a GraphQL query against a published subgraph
post.description:
The x402 settlement index on Base is subgraph `Cb56epg3EvQ6JRpPfknbkM54QxpzTvLa7mwKNQQfUyoj`. Its `payments` entities carry the receipts tashan joins to its catalogue: `to` (the receiver address), `amount` (USDC, 6 decimals) and `blockTimestamp`.

Aggregate rather than paginate where you can — this is a chain index, not a database, and a query that walks every payment will time out.

parameters.name: subgraphId
parameters.description: Deployment id of a subgraph published on The Graph Network

example.query: { payments(first: 5, orderBy: amount, orderDirection: desc, where: {to: "0xe9030014f5dae217d0a152f02a043567b16c1abf"}) { to amount blockTimestamp } }

200.description: GraphQL result. Note that GraphQL reports failures inside `errors` with HTTP 200, so check for it.

401.description: Missing or invalid gateway API key
